correctness.rationale: The two unfolded odds are A=r(1+b)/alpha and B=(1+rb)/(alpha*r), where 0<r<1 and 0<b<=1 for the ordered half-domain. A<1; while B<1 the order is preserved and r decreases by a factor at most 2r0/(1+r0)<1, contradicting B<1 once r<1/alpha. At the first B>=1, including equality, (r',b')=(AB,1/B), which lands in [0,4/alpha^2] x [0,1] and strictly preserves the physical ordering. The closed rectangle is an auxiliary continuous extension at zero odds, not an enlargement of the physical initial data. It is invariant and lands in the smaller rectangle with r<=min(5/32,4/alpha^2). In max{2alpha|dr|,|db|} the two Jacobian row bounds there are 55/64 and 3/4; the mean-value inequality and Banach give geometric convergence. Substitution gives the stated fixed point in the trap (r_*<=2/alpha^2<=1/8), with the announced physical coordinates. Swap symmetry handles the other half-domain.
